title: Write a tiny shell script
summary: A script saves commands so you can run them again. This one only prints a greeting and the current path.
introduction: A script saves commands so you can run them again. This one only prints a greeting and the current path. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain write a tiny shell script
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A script saves commands so you can run them again. This one only prints a greeting and the current path.

blocks.code:
printf '#!/bin/sh
printf "Hello, learner\n"
pwd
' > hello.sh
sh hello.sh
blocks.title: Write a tiny shell script

blocks.text: The script prints a greeting and the current directory. Using sh reads the script without needing executable permission.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the greeting in this practice script.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Read a script before running it; a file extension does not make it safe.
For more detail later, use this [Linux further reading](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html).
